reading: Fits a seeded gradient-boosting classifier and checks the smallest class before selecting stratified cross-validation for the regime labels.
Separates terrestrial solid tests from microgravity rows by phase before plotting the evidence lanes. The chart also keeps partial-gravity analogs in a separate selection.
Documents a proposed PSI/NTRS ingestion and AI architecture. The tracked AI, DATA, FRONTEND and backend files are one-byte placeholders, so there is no implementation to run here.
Normalizes the researcher's airflow, scale, focus and data-availability weights before ranking experiments. The result includes each component so a rank can be explained.
Compares BASS and Saffire records dimension by dimension, sorting values into shared, changed or unreported conditions. It separately lists recorded outcomes and cross-family caveats.
Tests the specified target against a recorded condition using a numerical tolerance or token coverage for categorical text. Each match carries the value and rule used.
Filters model-proposed citation IDs against the documents actually sent. It drops unsupported points and switches the response to abstention if the surviving evidence is insufficient.
Stores an explanatory comparison of dimensionless groups, including the Péclet formula and authored Earth and microgravity ranges. This module supplies static teaching data.
The entire tracked project is a two-line README identifying the challenge. There is no application, dataset or simulation to inspect at this revision.
Advances the active mission simulation by the checked time step, serializes the new state, and increments mission and game time within the transaction.
Loads one mission's saved simulation by kind and returns its current status, raising a missing-simulation error for an unknown run. This is the state-management layer of the NOVA game.
The NOVA game service checks that a mission exists and has a simulation, then rejects locked missions or a second active run before starting the requested one.
A reset removes the stored mission simulation inside a transaction, emits a reset event and starts a new run. This is the same NOVA service family seen in the related repositories.
Translates heterogeneous table cells into a model record. It skips blank cells, parses numerical values and units, and keeps bounded text context for the remaining fields.
Applies a droplet D-squared loss only when diameter and time trajectories are present. For a static row it returns a differentiable zero, so that missing trajectory cannot constrain the model.

A fenced Python example builds a Gemini question from JSON experiment context and the selected environment. It lives in the development guide. The tracked app.py and psi_data.json are both zero bytes.
Computes the selected oxygen partial pressure and divides it by a reference ISS partial pressure. The UI receives the ratio, units and arithmetic behind the comparison.
Compares numeric experiment fields only when both values exist, rounding both to six decimal places to check agreement. The comparison carries the field's label and unit.
Loops over requested gravity levels or a supplied default sweep and runs the combustion solver on a 40-cell grid setting for each level, yielding modeled responses to gravity changes.
Computes additive contributions for oxygen, pressure, gravity, material baseline and oxygen index using hand-set coefficients. The feature explanation in this file is deterministic.
Maps user gravity to a rounded index on the material's precomputed gravity curve. The nearby regime lookup applies fixed offsets for the chosen fuel and diluent.
Animates an already matched local answer in a timed chat transition and attaches that answer's source list. This code path displays a prepared response.
Scores browser knowledge entries against normalized question phrases and tokens, giving phrase matches and uncommon terms extra weight before choosing context.
Loads JSON evidence cards into the first ranking tier. Missing or falsey oxygen minima take a 21% default, an important assumption for reuse of the ranking.
Combines vector and keyword result lanes using reciprocal-rank fusion; the searcher can subsequently rerank results. This is retrieval logic independent of answer generation.
Converts normal and inverse CFI-G table rows into experiment records. Numeric parsing collects field-level quality issues, and the run ID preserves the PSI accession and test identifier.
GitHub reported this repository was empty at the review date. There were no committed files to examine.
Has separate parsers for BASS-II, BASS, Saffire and FLEX table layouts. The BASS-II parser explicitly maps native columns into the shared record format.
The client library filters evidence by enabled source and requires every search word to occur in the title/topic text. This is a local text filter over the supplied catalog.
Ranks text chunks with BM25 after query expansion, optionally restricts the pool to one investigation, and discards zero-score passages.
The FastAPI search endpoint accepts a query but returns a fixed FLEX-1 n-heptane example with the query interpolated into the note. The endpoint does not retrieve matching runs.
Fits normalized optical intensity as a function of time, adding penalties for predicted intensity below zero or above one to the mean-square observation error.
Excludes rejected findings and computes separate normalized severity, mission relevance, evidence-strength and actionability terms for the remaining records.
Selects FLEX neighbors of the same fuel and diluent by scaled oxygen and pressure differences. Counts extinction among those neighbors and summarizes their reported burn times.
Computes habitat match from the nearest available test values or reported ranges in oxygen, pressure, airflow and gravity, and includes a separate fuel applicability term in ranking.
Scores target oxygen against an investigation's reported interval, applies a preset partial-gravity factor, and combines environment fit with mission-pillar weights and recency.
Rescores each solid-fuel record under three prescribed scenario atmospheres by substituting mission oxygen and pressure, then passing the modified record to its hazard-index function.
Selects its estimator by prediction module. The ground module uses a seeded 300-tree random forest regressor and another regression path uses standardized ridge regression.
Predicts burning rate from measured training neighbors, downweighting distant conditions and giving the same fuel extra influence before forming the weighted mean.
Tries mixtures of the two classifiers' out-of-fold probabilities and selects the blend with the best macro-F1. The blend weight is tuned on validation predictions.
Fetches the requested experiments from SQL by ID. Its comparison sentence inserts the first two titles into fixed wording, so that sentence alone does not establish a measured difference.
The sole tracked README explicitly labels the dashboard a planning exercise. It lays out requirements for search and ranking without a runnable implementation.
Calls a Supabase vector-search function with the question embedding and a similarity threshold to retrieve experiment chunks for the answer.
Awards fixed points for a combustion-science classification and a microgravity experiment type and records reasons for those points. The score reflects authored priorities.
Ranks tests against a habitat using normalized Euclidean distance in target oxygen and pressure. The function takes a result limit and returns per-test relevance items.
Inspects each comparison field across selected records. A single null produces a missing-value status; otherwise it compares normalized text to distinguish shared from differing entries.
Computes an illustrative flame size from normalized oxygen, pressure, temperature, airflow and gravity using fixed coefficients and clamping. The output is an authored trend model.
Computes a detection difficulty score using gravity bands, low flow and the selected cool-flame scenario. The numerical increments are explicit heuristic choices.
Scores each investigation against the target gravity, then applies the configured atmosphere and airflow contributions. The exact-gravity match receives the highest gravity term.
Builds a BASS-II test-point table from a catalog, mapping pressure with its stated basis and pairing it with calibrated starting oxygen, material and source-page information.
Builds database test rows from study-specific column mappings, carrying test code, date, fuel, fuel class and configuration. A configured default can supply the fuel when a cell is blank.
Normalizes a scenario's pressure, oxygen, flow and material, checks feature ranges, and uses the model card and nearby experiment records when generating the prediction response.
Converts temperature and relative humidity into water-vapor mole fraction using saturation vapor pressure and total pressure. This feeds the modeled limiting oxygen calculation.
Compares oxygen with a material-specific limiting oxygen index to decide whether to render combustion, then uses gravity interpolation to set the displayed flame size and shape.
Creates a seeded synthetic PSI-themed training dataset and later exports fitted models. The generator's records are simulated examples, even though their experiment names refer to NASA programs.
Copies baseline telemetry and perturbs samples according to scenario severity and mission elapsed time. The injected signals support testing of the anomaly interface.
The Streamlit application renders local investigation and test-point tables. Its atlas filtering and risk-envelope sections explicitly mark the planned analysis features as placeholders.
Builds an evidence-score breakdown, adding reasons for high keyword overlap and scoring material agreement when the researcher supplied a material.
Requires sufficient coverage of query terms or an exact match in its lexical lane. A candidate found only by semantic retrieval must pass a higher similarity threshold.
Computes a material's limiting oxygen under selected flow, gravity, pressure and thickness. The resulting burn margin drives downstream probability and spread-rate functions.
The Cantera example couples inlet and exhaust mass-flow controllers around a reactor to control pressure while varying residence time. It is a combustion-library example.
Adds semantic retrieval only for selected qualitative query intents and checks the vector index against the active dataset fingerprint before using it.

Maps an input risk score to discrete decisions. Critical scores can produce an automatic cutoff decision, while intermediate warnings call for human confirmation. This is decision logic, not a hardware test.
GitHub reported this repository was empty at the review date. There were no committed files to examine.
Identifies phrases the ranking configuration could not interpret after subtracting recognized materials, presets, conditions and generic terms. These phrases can be exposed to the researcher.
Filters citation-like PSI IDs in an answer through the known identifiers. Its assistant endpoint accepts POST requests, validates the payload, and requires the configured model credential.

Parses BASS-II display text for blowoff, extinction or failed ignition and assigns sustained combustion by default otherwise. That default is an inferred label that needs checking against the original row.
Uses the tested oxygen range when available and otherwise a representative oxygen value, then checks pressure coverage. With no oxygen anchor the atmosphere term receives a fixed cap.
Requests a comparison by experiment IDs from the backend. If that request fails, it constructs the comparison from the matching records in its local benchmark collection.
The Streamlit dashboard requests JSON from a local HTTP backend with a five-second timeout and checks the health endpoint. Missing or unsuccessful responses return an unavailable result.
The comparison view preserves experimental units in its layout, but both record selectors are disabled and its measurement canvas is empty in this pinned implementation.
Calculates habitat distance by adding absolute oxygen and pressure gaps in their respective units. Any test missing either quantity receives no distance.
The command-line loop accepts scenario inputs with defaults, runs the predictor and prints its fields, including estimated soot and burn duration, alongside generated interpretation lines.
Creates a timestamped SQLite backup using a read-only source connection. This is working infrastructure code; it makes no combustion prediction.
Scores a candidate as matching condition fields divided by comparable fields and returns null when the denominator is zero. Unknown and incompatible fields keep separate counts.
Turns normalized inputs into flame-path widths, shear and colors for an illustrative SVG. Its morphology is a rendering rule rather than a measured spread endpoint.
Assigns a corroboration term from the number of distinct research groups, increases it in steps and applies a contradiction adjustment. Repeated findings from one group do not add independent groups.
The FLEX investigation note names an analysis JSON file, but that file and an analysis program are absent from the pinned tree. The release contains documentation and a license.
Describes a microgravity RAG assistant and starts virtual-environment setup instructions. The repository has a requirements file but no application or indexing code at this revision.
Vectorizes an expanded material query, computes cosine similarity and filters candidate materials by compatible class before returning matches from the experiment database.
Aggregates the archive inventory by file extension and sums byte sizes. Its analytics describe downloaded research material and storage coverage.
Generates scenario-specific synthetic telemetry. A dust case raises particulate readings, while a smoldering case moves a modeled hotspot along the demo sensor positions.
Preserves the distinction between calibrated Saffire duct flow and an instrument display. When flow is absent it looks up the BASS fan-display sequence under its own measurement type.
This is an engineer's profile linking to projects and a learning guide. The repository itself contains no executable fire-research implementation.
The README identifies a team-formation and planning phase. Source and notebook directories contain placeholders, alongside background and data-source documentation.
A database integration test attempts to update or delete already-reviewed evidence and checks the database response. It exercises the immutability boundary of published records.
Samples terrain along a specified direction to estimate the apparent local horizon for a lunar site. This supports landing-site analysis rather than combustion analysis.
Computes the Sun and Earth's apparent local directions for a lunar location using astronomical vectors and the Moon's orientation for the requested date.
Probes remote 3D model assets with a timeout before selecting a usable model for the scene. This supplies viewer resilience rather than a flame-physics solver.
The sole tracked file specifies natural-language experiment search, ranking, metadata and result display. These are project goals in a design document.
Combines a finding's oxygen, pressure and gravity match for the chosen scenario with configured relevance, severity and evidence weights before sorting the findings.
Parses material text into a shape and thickness for solid-sample matching, including explicit inch-to-millimetre conversions for rod sizes. This makes geometry a separate comparison input.
Builds a query vector from a bilingual feature vocabulary and searches the document matrix, with an optional document-type filter. Unsupported vocabulary contributes no matrix features.
Builds a per-experiment heuristic risk breakdown from fields including fuel, limiting oxygen, temperature and burning-rate data. The numerical score is produced by explicit domain rules.
Tokenizes a query, optionally obtains classifier probabilities and applies record filters before combining signals to retrieve matches from the local evidence collection.
Computes equal and opposite heat transfers between a room's two layers based on their temperature difference and wall area. This is compartment-scale model code in CFAST.
Adjusts a base limiting oxygen index for pressure, CO₂ and a term that increases as forced draft decreases. The result feeds its telemetry evaluation and estimated flame temperature.
Gives full match credit inside a tested interval, decays the score outside it and preserves unavailable input as missing. Material aliases and mission pillars contribute separate ranking factors.
Compares the habitat's oxygen with each investigation's reported range and returns a reason for coverage or the gap. Pressure and the requested pillar also enter the ranking path.
GitHub reported this repository was empty at the review date. There were no committed files to examine.
Organizes NASA reference tables by topic, including BASS/Saffire solids, SAME smoke and FLEX suppression. The pinned tree ships experimental CSVs and planning notes, with no executable analysis file.
Builds chart points from source-run oxygen and airflow or CO; excludes nonnumeric pairs and, by default, CO with a disputed qualifier, rows marked for oxygen review and zero display airflow.
Checks numeric feature bounds, standardizes values, and applies fitted feature weights. It returns the prediction with the list of out-of-range inputs and uses a sigmoid for classification models.
The chat adds the selected experiment, material, gravity, active filters and user-entered conditions to a question. A follow-up can therefore refer to the current screen.
The habitat calculator models a cylinder with hemispherical end caps. It converts wall thickness to metres and estimates hoop stress, shell mass and the mass of the cabin atmosphere separately.

Project README describing a BASS-II explorer, per-test quality flags and a comparison workflow. The pinned tree contains the project description and banner rather than the advertised application code.
Two-line project description proposing an AI research platform for microgravity combustion. The pinned tree has no application source to assess.
The comparison distinguishes a missing lower or upper bound from a measured range and computes the intersection of complete ranges. Nonoverlap and incomplete evidence have distinct outcomes.
The extraction sanitizer checks each numeric draft field against a quote in the submitted excerpt. Missing or unmatched quotes clear that field and record why it was dropped.
The comparison link deduplicates requested IDs and admits only reviewer-verified solid-flammability records. It returns a separate list of IDs that failed that check.
The ingestion script converts a combustion PDF to Markdown without images and splits the text for indexing. A figure containing the only numerical result would need a separate extraction path.
The Flame Lab draws the tested interval inside its slider and announces whether the current value is inside that interval. It also provides a distinct message for controls with no test data.

A material-specific coefficient sets simulated spread speed and two fixed thresholds set hazard classes. The displayed test-log identifier is assembled from airflow and material text, so it cannot independently identify a source record.
The front-end prototype decodes embedded geometry and parses the enclosure into Three.js meshes. This is a hardware visualization, with geometry supplied in the page.
The scenario helper calculates oxygen partial pressure from the entered oxygen percentage and total pressure. It returns this separately from the scenario scores.
The retrieval service provides a direct SQLite text-search fallback if the vector store lacks records, where it ranks experiments by overlapping query terms instead of vector distance.
The single-line app.py is a French comment explaining where Streamlit orchestration would go. The separate physics and data-loader modules in this revision are also placeholders.
The offline assistant prepares a structured evidence summary with search results. Its displayed response identifies this deterministic mode separately from an optional AI selection step.
The vision code processes HSV image channels, applying local contrast enhancement to dim blue-flame regions. This is an image-conditioning step, not an absolute temperature measurement.

The educational model assigns a cool-flame visualization and prompts the user to switch to heat vision after the visible flame disappears. Its wording teaches the distinction between visibility and continued reaction.

The numerical citation check converts pressure units and tests both fraction and percentage representations. A rounded decimal claim can match a more precise reference, while unlabelled integer counts must match exactly.
The FLEX prediction service compares a request’s oxygen fraction against its historical training envelope and reports an out-of-range condition before presenting a droplet estimate.
The comparison screen plots the tested oxygen envelopes for selected investigations, so a reader can inspect experimental coverage alongside the attribute table.
The BASS-II extractor finds Appendix A tables and locates the observation column from PDF word coordinates. Extraction depends on the column heading and its position on each page.
The normalization pipeline distinguishes normal from inverse flames while creating Flame Design records. The two feed configurations remain identifiable after conversion to the shared catalog.
The synthesis service enriches returned experiment references with fields from its local database and falls back to its deterministic ranking when model-based synthesis is unavailable.

The habitat navigator reports ground limiting-oxygen-index thresholds with their test pressures. Its response explicitly identifies their 1-g origin when the selected habitat has different conditions.
This is a profile README. Its PyroGravity entry describes a team prototype for comparing microgravity combustion experiments, while the implementation is outside this profile repository.
The comparator calls a quiescent-versus-forced-flow change major. It separately categorizes gravity differences by a hard-coded microgravity threshold and relative distance.
The offline insight engine routes question terms to lists of ranked results and formats each score with its reasons. This gives a reproducible fallback when a hosted model is unavailable.
The service intersects the reported variable ranges across investigations and returns explicit overlap limits. A missing bound is handled before performing the numerical comparison.
The reconnaissance script queries NASA NTRS for selected combustion topics, keys results by report ID and constructs a direct citation URL for each catalog entry.
The bundled dashboard restores the previous catalog question when a user returns from the research guide and retains the active question before handling the next turn.
GitHub reported this repository was empty at the review date. There were no committed files to examine.
The gold-layer pipeline assigns each finding a score and named components using sample count, quality, agreement and closeness inputs. The resulting evidence rank is a team-designed scoring judgment.

The verifier checks extracted insight cells against document text and treats half-empty field/source pairs as errors. It distinguishes absent entries from entries that claim evidence without completing the pair.
The catalog builder writes a compact CSV from a tracked PSI manifest using a specified field list. Missing manifest keys are exported as empty strings.
The droplet module represents radiative heat loss increasing with droplet size to drive a modeled cool-flame transition. The transition is an output of the model assumptions.
The comparison handler accepts investigator-supplied weights, maximum result count and minimum coverage, then passes those controls to the shared experiment ranker.
The dashboard separates the investigation explorer from its data-quality and supplied-risk-index screens. Duplicate counts are displayed separately from the reported mean index.
The query engine inspects a column’s type before aggregating and rejects sum, mean or median on nonnumeric fields instead of silently treating labels as measurements.
The material comparison gives the Nomex/starter specimen special treatment because consumption of the igniter and ignition of the target material are different outcomes.
The evidence generator builds a dataset-dependent oxygen-depletion finding and attaches source metadata. The magnitude displayed therefore depends on which observations are loaded.
The single-page dashboard wires material and gravity selections to a recalculated relative fire-risk display. Its material buttons show the chosen limiting oxygen index.
The shared comparison state adds an experiment ID only once and removes it by ID. Multiple screens can manage the same comparison selection.
The pinned README gives the project title and challenge name. There is no committed application logic to assess.
The document pipeline routes Office files through conversion before extracting PDF pages. It reports which path was used so page references retain a reproducible origin.
A browser rule declares flame propagation for oxygen at or above 30% and pressure at or below 10.3, then derives a confidence number from oxygen. That number comes from the branch formula.
The build script normalizes fourteen NASA PSI experiment-table CSVs into web assets. The transformation is a separate reproducible input stage for the browser dashboard.
The BASS-II cleaner parses the airflow progression into an ordered list of steps and extracts event flags rather than forcing a multi-step run into a single velocity.
The simulator uses nearest-neighbor prediction and coverage checks for a FLEX query, then uses a diameter-squared burn model and a separate cool-phase duration to drive the animation.
The combustion API serves a curated benchmark dataset and exposes research highlights via a separate route. Clients receive the previously assembled entries rather than recomputation from raw traces.
The spread-rate builder transcribes the BASS-II report’s Table 5.1 and explicitly excludes M6 and M12, whose rates were not tracked. Missing measurements therefore do not become zero-speed examples.
The design repository supplies a JSON Schema for a simulation response, including provenance and a direct PSI or NTRS source URL. This is an interface contract rather than a running simulator.
The copilot entry point validates a model answer and exposes whether the result came from the model, a fallback or an error. A rejected answer can surface the problems found by validation.
The local search multiplies query term counts by inverse document frequency, calculates normalized similarities against document vectors and returns the highest positive-scoring records.
The opposed-flow spread model explicitly describes its U-shaped oxygen limit as illustrative. It provides a mechanism demonstration with assumed constants rather than a fitted lunar threshold.
The dashboard’s overview builds its fire-risk tile from a fixed LOW status and trend text. That tile is a demonstration value, not a measurement derived from a live detector.

The shape comparison selects among six airflow transformations using inner-fold log loss, then evaluates the selected logistic model on an outer fold. This tests the model-selection procedure as well as the chosen formula.
A safety rule combines scaled oxygen enrichment with a second ratio using explicit 70/30 weights. Its output is a constructed severity score, distinct from a measured probability.
The Streamlit method note explains that investigations are rated from zero to five on eight criteria and weighted for a chosen need. The ranking communicates the team’s priorities.
The SIBAL classifier holds out entire physical tests during validation, so the starting and final airflow observations of a single burn cannot be split across training and evaluation.

The Spanish technical guide distinguishes solid-fuel ignition studies, gaseous flame research and smoke detection. It explains why a detector response depends on the smoke source and particle properties.
The normalization job retains rows with missing flame-off times and logs their missing-value status. Repeated problems are summarized by investigation, field, raw value and issue code.
The retriever combines dense cosine scores with BM25 and ranks the combined scores. Selection logic then limits how many passages are retained for the answer.
The PDF importer falls back to image OCR where needed and records an OCR failure rather than presenting an empty extraction as verified source text.
The evidence service implements a coverage query scoped to its local corpus and attaches the dataset ID. Coverage counts therefore refer to that indexed corpus.

The predictor labeled PINN scales a tabulated burning constant by oxygen and pressure and calculates heat-up and extinction with explicit equations. The function defaults an unrecognized fuel to heptane.
The experimental-table normalizer emits different geometry labels for inverse and normal spherical burner flames. The distinction survives export into the common table.
The engine returns scenario scores, matched examples and risk text, and identifies its own provider as a versioned rules engine. The answer path runs locally through this rule set.
The comparison workspace counts unknown controlled conditions separately from the conditions it can compare. Missing fields remain visible when judging whether two experiments form a usable pair.
The chat inserts the user’s question, creates a conversation ID when needed and submits against that conversation. The handling for the first turn differs from an existing chat.

The physics service maps material names to preset flammability factors and assigns a generic coefficient when it cannot identify the material. Predictions for unidentified materials inherit this default.
The NetworkX graph can return a bounded-hop neighborhood around a named node. It lets a researcher follow local links without pulling the entire experiment graph into the visualization.
The experiment comparison labels its chart as a screening view, hides oxygen outside its screening range and identifies values omitted from the chart.
A README links to the Flame in Freefall challenge. No pinned application source, datasets or model implementation accompany it.
The retriever fuses ranked BM25 hits across queries using reciprocal rank. An experiment passage can gain rank by appearing in several result lists.
The nearest-neighbor predictor uses the outcomes of nearby ISS runs, takes times only from neighbors that reported them and reports when pressure stretches past historical coverage.
The typed dataset record includes a flag for partial-gravity bounding models or references. This permits a model-derived comparison to remain distinct from an underlying experiment.
The flammability-map component filters liquid-droplet observations separately from other fuel classes. Changing this switch changes which points are plotted.
The FLEX importer retains scientific anomalies as warnings. The records remain available for inspection rather than disappearing from the processed table.
The Three.js renderer updates shader parameters from scenario conditions, converting oxygen percent to a fraction. It renders a changing flame appearance rather than measuring flame speed.

The PSI-117 analysis fits pressure trends separately to experimental values with and without duplicates and to simulated values. It also computes the percentage difference between model and measured means.
The comparator records that gravity is an investigation-level designation and not a measured acceleration for each test. Its comparison result carries that qualification forward.

The browser chatbot selects source links from NASA knowledge entries whose retrieval score is at least 60% of the strongest hit. The displayed references therefore depend on relative retrieval scores.
The research retriever tracks how many passages it has selected per source and limits repeated selections, preventing one source from filling the entire result list.
The simulation module identifies its local-emitter field as a dimensionless educational visualization. Its values do not constitute a calibrated combustion or CFD result.
The investigation router recognizes smoke, detectors, aerosol terminology and individual source materials in the query. These keywords influence which investigation receives the question.
The decision-tree trainer defines its target as the recorded end of a FLEX droplet test. A prediction about that label should not be transferred to sustained spread on a fabric specimen.
The 3D reaction–diffusion demonstrator introduces upward transport when gravity is present. This term changes the modeled shape separately from the initial oxygen distribution.
NASA’s program repository describes the global challenge and points participants to the discussion forum and registration. It supplies organizer context, not a competing combustion application.
The retrieval evaluator explains how it scores changes in chunk size without relying on unstable chunk IDs. The question set includes two items whose answers are absent from the indexed reports.
The single-page audit uses ideal-gas cabin moles to calculate the effect of a specified CO₂ discharge and the extinguisher mass corresponding to a target CO₂ fraction.

The numerical helper computes a finite-difference gradient along a chosen array axis and selects the upwind stencil from the velocity direction. This supports directional transport on the simulation grid.
The PMMA rod implementation evaluates the report’s quench-limit correlation and derives the location of its minimum. The domain in the file is rods at one atmosphere.
The Streamlit simulation assigns qualitative airflow bands and risk messages using numerical thresholds. Its critical-airflow status is a software decision rule.
The chart shows each investigation’s reported value as a bar, and labels both the tooltip and vertical axis with the parameter unit. It does not silently rescale unlike units.
GitHub reported this repository was empty at the review date. There were no committed files to examine.
The BRE dissertation importer detects when a single flame appears in two source tables and retains the designated record for that flame. The code names the overlapping flame ID explicitly.
The droplet model generation script discloses that the per-study model was selected after examining its evaluation scores. The reported score is therefore optimistic as a fresh-test estimate.
The data-quality function computes the fraction of populated study IDs, titles and objectives. This measures metadata completeness and does not test the scientific validity of the records.
The comparability engine identifies a scale mismatch between BASS-II’s duct and Saffire-I’s much wider configuration, then explains that constraint before treating the two results as comparable.
The question endpoint enforces input length, checks its exact-question answer cache, then rate-limits by client address before calling the configured model with investigation data.
This profile README links to a separate Flame in Freefall project repository and live demo. The profile itself supplies a pointer rather than a second implementation.
The explanation service chooses an audience profile and asks the model for a structured JSON response. It constructs the explanation prompt around retrieved PSI material.
The oxygen component awards no points when the tested range is unknown, and returns a reason alongside the points used in scenario ranking.
A lunar query takes a preset investigation-priority path. Other questions use fuzzy search with a score cutoff of 0.42 and respect the requested result limit.
The physics module returns separate diffusion and convection timescales with explanatory results. These are computed quantities rather than measured burn durations.
The search scorer builds title text from the experiment name, abbreviation and PSI ID, and searches other fields including platform, gravity context, findings, fuels and sensors.
The applicability check tests within-category feature ranges, then measures nearest-neighbor distance using the training split’s normalization before accepting a test point.
This author-profile README points readers to a separate Ignis μ challenge repository among unrelated portfolio projects. The profile entry is a link to the implementation.
For the methanol chart the script multiplies the entered oxygen by a fixed series of coefficients. The source identifies these values as prototype demonstration data.
The scenario validation script asks a classifier for a risk class and probability and a regressor for an extinction estimate, clipping that prediction to a minimum of 0.1.
The ranking explanation handles ties explicitly and identifies up to two weighted dimensions that most increase the first record’s score relative to the second.
The ask endpoint parses bracketed citation IDs, splits combined references, normalizes the case and separates references absent from the records sent to the model.
The ranking route echoes the submitted research question and returns an empty ranked-item list. This endpoint is a placeholder at this revision.
The evidence grader allows a passage with one overlapping question word or two retrieved runs to proceed; that gate tests retrieval sufficiency, not whether a sentence is supported.
The retained LICENSE gives MIT software-permission terms. It supplies no experiment, training method or result to assess in this repository.
Ensemble inference computes a mean extinction probability and lower and upper quantiles from component predictions, alongside a distance check against fitted inputs.
A numeric condition’s similarity decays exponentially with absolute mismatch. The row score is then scaled by the record’s confidence before relevance is displayed.
The calibration service estimates grid-line deviations and fits a homography to detected corners. Its residuals quantify image geometry in pixels rather than flame speed.
The inspected API router exposes a health check returning an OK status. This route verifies availability rather than performing combustion analysis.
The data module pairs keyword groups such as oxygen, ventilation and lunar habitats with hand-authored findings. The text documents the answers supplied for those topics.
This portfolio helper filters unpublished posts and sorts the remaining posts for display. It is a publishing component rather than a fire-data analysis.
A ranking component returns zero condition fit without usable oxygen and pressure. Evidence strength separately combines provenance tier, stated oxygen fraction and a log-scaled card count.
The workflow CLI prints which specialists ran, elapsed time and per-step errors, then lists limitations and exits with status 2 if any step failed.
The combustion solver numerically finds the flame temperature at which the enthalpy increment equals supplied net heat, using a bracketed root finder and a stated upper temperature bound.
The ISS scene converts a burning module’s heat-release rate into a temperature input using an 0.85 factor and the module’s volume. The display is driven by this model.
Exploration relevance starts from 35 points and rewards oxygen-rich, low-pressure conditions. Absent oxygen and pressure are replaced with 21 and 101.3 kPa before scoring.
The two-line README describes intended paper summaries and experiment comparison. It contains no method, scoring rule or validation result.
The evidence-gap routine first requires named input columns, narrows to BASS-II, and groups rows only after dropping entries missing the factor or its contextual variables.
Extinction classification stores out-of-fold probabilities for each candidate model. Unless split indices are supplied, the implementation partitions by group to keep related rows together.
The categorizer maps strings containing aerosol, smoke or dust to an aerosol category. These are text-derived labels for the index.
Trial ranking links observations to trials, records why a study is excluded and rejects synthetic trials unless the request explicitly permits them.
The README describes a NASA PSI dashboard for exploring and ranking investigations. This revision supplies a description rather than an inspectable ranking implementation.
The inference module compares a standardized query with saved training neighbors and flags queries beyond a saved distance limit as outside the fitted domain.
The ranking screen sorts precomputed candidates by final score, uses rank as a tiebreaker, then limits the displayed subset to the requested number.
The atmosphere distance is zero inside each investigation’s oxygen and pressure ranges. Outside the ranges it combines oxygen and pressure deviations on scales of 15 and 40.
The FastAPI application mounts separate investigation and analyst routers. The root endpoint supplies an online service status independently of either research route.
The ranking module assigns separate evidence components for flow, smoke detection and data availability; flow variation and merely having a flow column earn different values.
The interactive renderer sets target flame radius from a gravity-dependent constant, square root of fuel rate and oxygen relative to 21 percent. This is an animation mapping.
The README identifies a planned condition-aware evidence tool and directs readers to dependency-ordered work packages. It describes the repository as specifications and planning.
The ask handler requires a safety question, chooses preset experiment context with ACME as fallback, and builds a prompt using the selected environment.
Extinction classifiers are compared under randomized stratified and grouped fivefold splits. The script computes recall, precision, F1, accuracy and ROC AUC for each setup.

The spread predictor fits a regularized model to log-transformed spread rates. The displayed training error is computed on the fitting inputs, and prediction also applies a fuel-specific oxygen floor.
